notes: Examined both guards of the form `require(IAlchemechNFT(_nft).ownerOf(_tokenId) == msg.sender)`. The address the guard reads its answer from is the caller-supplied `_nft`, which is what the predicate reports -- but each guard sits inside `if (_nft == alchemechNFT)` or `if (_nft == patronNFT)`, comparisons against state variables, and the `else` branch reverts. So at the point of the guard, `_nft` can only be one of two addresses the contract itself holds, and the caller cannot substitute a contract it controls. The guard is sound. Not an instance of access_control at this location. This says nothing about the rest of the file.
